sim.identity: Harborlight Stories / 海光影业 · Hangzhou · Independent producer. Chen Lin, co-founder and development lead, prepares the slate; the founder approves production spend. A US freelance story editor reviews dialogue and cultural context.
sim.audienceBody: US English-speaking women aged 25–44; romance with capable heroines. Hypothetical audience intent, not measured demographics. Seek a platform licensing partner; no existing US distribution agreement or owned consumer app.
sim.resourcesBody: Eight-person core team; strong contemporary romance experience, two controllable interiors and a bilingual script editor. No established US casting or location partner. Planning assumptions: $15k development cap, $180k production ceiling per title, 10 shoot days, 6 principal cast, no stunts/VFX. Budgets are invented case constraints, not market benchmarks.
sim.slateBody: Three unproduced original concepts, no footage, no licenses sold. Working format: 40 × 90-second episodes, subject to buyer feedback. English originals are preferred over dubbing for this experiment. Avoid child performers, medical claims and expensive public locations. Buyer terms, acquisition costs and revenue are unknown.

Neither proves why audiences watched, US demand, profitability, or buyer appetite. A useful next step connects a specific story device to your script, your constraints, and a test that could reject the idea.
sim.contract.name: The Exit Clause
sim.contract.premise: An indebted event planner agrees to a staged engagement, then discovers the contract gives her control of the family business if the groom walks away.
sim.contract.fit: Best first development candidate under these invented constraints: adult cast, office/apartment interiors, and a recurring negotiation engine. Her bargaining power needs to drive the romance.
sim.contract.risk: A legal twist may require too much explanation. A familiar billionaire setup needs a distinctive heroine goal; a synopsis cannot demonstrate audience appetite.
sim.contract.test: Table-read both openings with five target-language readers. Ask them to retell her leverage and choose which question makes them want episode 3. Small qualitative test, not demand validation.
sim.receipt.name: The Last Receipt
sim.receipt.premise: A hotel bookkeeper framed for theft returns as the anonymous buyer of the hotel, but the only witness who can clear her is her former fiancé.
sim.receipt.fit: A concrete evidence trail gives each episode a reveal. A dressed office can double as hotel administration; a luxury lobby and crowds would exceed this case’s location plan.
sim.receipt.risk: Revenge could crowd out the romance. Hotel scale may exceed the budget; buyer interest and production quotes remain unverified.
sim.receipt.test: Rewrite the pilot using only two interiors. Ask a line producer for a scene-level estimate and readers whether they believe her evidence is strong enough to act.
sim.midnight.name: Before Midnight, Again
sim.midnight.premise: A night-shift concierge repeats the hour before a tenant disappears. Each reset saves a clue but erases one memory of the man helping her.
sim.midnight.fit: A contained supernatural romance offers a different slate option. Repeated sets help, but continuity and consistent reset rules require more development effort.
sim.midnight.risk: The reset may confuse viewers in 90 seconds. Disappearance scenes must stay off-screen to avoid action costs; differentiation does not establish commercial potential.
sim.midnight.test: Storyboard the reset without VFX. Test whether readers can state what persists and what is lost; hold production until the rules survive a cold read.
sim.contract.script:
EPISODE 1 — OFFICE, NIGHT
MAYA places an unpaid invoice between herself and ADRIAN.
MAYA: You want a fiancée. I want my crew paid. Those are different contracts.
ADRIAN: Thirty days. Two dinners. No one gets hurt.
She crosses out a paragraph.
MAYA: Then why does this say I owe you if I leave?
He slides over a pen.
ADRIAN: Write something fair.
MAYA: Whoever walks away loses control.
His smile disappears when she turns to the signature page.
CUT: Both signatures sit beneath the company seal.

EPISODE 2 — OFFICE, MORNING
Adrian’s sister EVE reads the agreement.
EVE: You used the shareholder template?
MAYA: He said write something fair.
EVE calls Adrian. Speakerphone.
ADRIAN: Last night was a mistake. We’re done.
Eve covers the phone and points to a clause.
EVE: If he terminates, your proxy activates.
MAYA looks at the invoice, then the board meeting invitation.
MAYA: Tell him I’ll see him at nine.
The phone lights up: BOARD VOTE — REMOVE MAYA’S CREW.
sim.receipt.script:
EPISODE 1 — HOTEL ACCOUNTS OFFICE, DAY
NORA returns her staff badge. Manager GRANT drops a receipt on the desk.
GRANT: Your signature. Missing cash. Be grateful we’re keeping this quiet.
NORA: That printer was replaced on Tuesday. This is dated Monday.
He tears the receipt in half.
GRANT: Then prove it.
Nora pockets the lower half. Outside, her phone rings.
LAWYER (PHONE): The purchase closed. Do you want the staff told who owns the hotel?
NORA: Not yet.

EPISODE 2 — SAME OFFICE, EVENING
Nora requests the archived printer log. Her former fiancé ELI blocks the cabinet.
ELI: If Grant sees you, you’re finished.
NORA: He already finished me. Move.
Eli opens the cabinet. The folder is empty except for an envelope bearing his name.
NORA: You signed the report?
ELI: I signed to keep you out of court.
She unfolds a copy. The timestamp matches the torn receipt.
NORA: Then why did you sign it before the money disappeared?
sim.midnight.script:
EPISODE 1 — APARTMENT CONCIERGE DESK, NIGHT
11:59. JO finds a key with a red thread. BEN arrives, breathless.
BEN: Don’t give that to room twelve.
JO: You said that yesterday.
BEN: No. I said it in the last hour.
The desk phone rings. A woman whispers: He’s outside my door.
Jo reaches for the emergency button. Midnight. Blackout.
11:00. The lights return. The red thread is tied around Jo’s wrist.
Ben enters.
JO: Do I know you?

EPISODE 2 — CONCIERGE DESK, NIGHT
Ben sets down a notebook in Jo’s handwriting.
JO reads: Objects in my pocket stay. Memories of Ben don’t.
JO: Convenient story.
She tears a corner off a blank page and puts it in her pocket.
BEN: We have fifty-eight minutes.
JO: Then we use them to find her.
The phone rings early. Same woman.
WOMAN: This time don’t trust the man at your desk.
Jo looks down. Ben has the matching red thread around his wrist.

montage.title: 60-second ad
montage.intro: Joins a hook, two to four strong scenes and a cliff from this title's ad clips into one vertical ad of up to 60 seconds: hard cuts in story order, the sound brought to one loudness, nothing added to the picture. Nothing after the spoiler line is used. The ad appears in Clips as “Ad · 60 s”, to download or to use in Launch like any clip.
montage.none.hint: Made from this title's existing ad clips; nothing is spent.
montage.building.hint: Joining {n} pieces into one file ({length}): usually a minute or two. This part of the page refreshes on its own.
montage.exists: This ad is already built from the current clips; it is the first one below.
montage.refused.no_clips: This title has no ad clips yet. Cut clips on its episodes first, then build the 60-second ad.
montage.refused.too_few: A 60-second ad needs a hook, at least two scenes and a cliff: four separate moments from before the spoiler line. Usable clips so far: {n}. Cut clips on more of its early episodes, then try again.
montage.cannotBuild: You can watch and download these ads; building one needs edit rights on this title.
montage.failed.render_failed: The ad could not be joined from its clips. Press Build again; if it fails twice, tell Pulsar staff.
montage.failed.stopped: The build stopped before it finished. Press Build again.
